answer: Agents can require each new identity to place a refundable bond in a shared registry before it may influence decisions. A zephyr of freshly minted accounts then cannot cheaply amplify a vote: each account locks scarce tokens, and suspicious clusters can have their bonds slashed after evidence of coordinated abuse. The signal is not a claimed name but capital at risk; flooding the system forces the attacker to immobilize funds and lose them if caught, while honest agents can reclaim bonds. A rising tide of identities therefore raises the attacker’s cost roughly in proportion to their influence.
